            {
              type: [32m'text'[39m,
              text: [32m'# Cascading Soft-Delete, Global Read Scoping and Archive Recovery (Ash Framework v3)\n'[39m +
                [32m'\n'[39m +
                [32m'## Background\n'[39m +
                [32m'\n'[39m +
                [32m'`/home/user/forum` holds a Mix project (OTP app `:forum`) for a discussion-forum backend built on the\n'[39m +
                [32m'Ash Framework v3 (`ash 3.31.0`). Content is three levels deep: a post owns comments, and a comment\n'[39m +
                [32m'owns reactions.\n'[39m +
                [32m'\n'[39m +
                [32m'Deleting content in this product is never destructive: removed content stays in storage, stays\n'[39m +
                [32m'invisible to ordinary readers, can be inspected by an administrator, and can be recovered later.\n'[39m +
                [32m'Recovery has to be *precise* — undoing a deletion must bring back exactly what that deletion removed\n'[39m +
                [32m'and must not resurrect content that had already been deleted by an earlier, unrelated operation.\n'[39m +
                [32m'\n'[39m +
                [32m'The project currently contains only the domain shell and the project configuration. Everything\n'[39m +
                [32m'described below is missing and must be built.\n'[39m +
                [32m'\n'[39m +
                [32m'## Requirements\n'[39m +
                [32m'\n'[39m +
                [32m'### Domain and resources\n'[39m +
                [32m'\n'[39m +
                [32m'The domain module `Forum.Content` (`lib/forum/content.ex`) must expose exactly these three\n'[39m +
                [32m'resources, each using `Ash.DataLayer.Ets` configured with `private? true`:\n'[39m +
                [32m'\n'[39m +
                [32m'| Module                   | File                            | Own attribute                         |\n'[39m +
                [32m'| ------------------------ | ------------------------------- | ------------------------------------- |\n'[39m +
                [32m'| `Forum.Content.Post`     | `lib/forum/content/post.ex`     | `title` — `:string`, public, required |\n'[39m +
                [32m'| `Forum.Content.Comment`  | `lib/forum/content/comment.ex`  | `body` — `:string`, public, required  |\n'[39m +
                [32m'| `Forum.Content.Reaction` | `lib/forum/content/reaction.ex` | `emoji` — `:string`, public, required |\n'[39m +
                [32m'\n'[39m +
                [32m'Every one of the three resources also has:\n'[39m +
                [32m'\n'[39m +
                [32m'* a primary key attribute named `id` of type `:uuid`, generated by default;\n'[39m +
                [32m'* a public attribute `archived_at` of type `:utc_datetime_usec`, `nil` for live records;\n'[39m +
                [32m'* a public attribute `archive_batch_id` of type `:uuid`, `nil` for live records.\n'[39m +
                [32m'\n'[39m +
                [32m'Relationships:\n'[39m +
                [32m'\n'[39m +
                [32m'* `Forum.Content.Post` — a to-many relationship named `:comments` pointing at\n'[39m +
                [32m'  `Forum.Content.Comment`.\n'[39m +
                [32m'* `Forum.Content.Comment` — a to-one relationship named `:post` pointing at `Forum.Content.Post`,\n'[39m +
                [32m'  backed by a required and externally writable foreign-key attribute `post_id`; and a to-many\n'[39m +
                [32m'  relationship named `:reactions` pointing at `Forum.Content.Reaction`.\n'[39m +
                [32m'* `Forum.Content.Reaction` — a to-one relationship named `:comment` pointing at\n'[39m +
                [32m'  `Forum.Content.Comment`, backed by a required and externally writable foreign-key attribute\n'[39m +
                [32m'  `comment_id`.\n'[39m +
                [32m'\n'[39m +
                [32m'Aggregates:\n'[39m +
                [32m'\n'[39m +
                [32m'* `Forum.Content.Post` must expose a public `count` aggregate named `comment_count` over `:comments`.\n'[39m +
                [32m'* `Forum.Content.Comment` must expose a public `count` aggregate named `reaction_count` over\n'[39m +
                [32m'  `:reactions`.\n'[39m +
                [32m'\n'[39m +
                [32m'### Actions\n'[39m +
                [32m'\n'[39m +
                [32m'All three resources must define these seven actions under exactly these names:\n'[39m +
                [32m'\n'[39m +
                [32m'| Name             | Action type                                           | Input                                                                                                             |\n'[39m +
                [32m'| ---------------- | ----------------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |\n'[39m +
                [32m"| `:create`        | create                                                | the resource's own required attribute plus its foreign key (`post_id` for a comment, `comment_id` for a reaction) |\n"[39m +
                [32m"| `:read`          | read (**must be the resource's primary read action**) | none                                                                                                              |\n"[39m +
                [32m'| `:archived`      | read                                                  | none                                                                                                              |\n'[39m +
                [32m'| `:with_archived` | read                                                  | none                                                                                                              |\n'[39m +
                [32m'| `:archive`       | destroy                                               | none                                                                                                              |\n'[39m +
                [32m'| `:restore`       | update                                                | none                                                                                                              |\n'[39m +
                [32m'| `:purge`         | destroy                                               | none                                                                                                              |\n'[39m +
                [32m'\n'[39m +
                [32m'"Input: none" is binding: each of those actions must succeed when invoked with an empty parameter\n'[39m +
                [32m'map and no additional arguments, e.g. `Ash.Query.for_read(Forum.Content.Post, :with_archived, %{})`,\n'[39m +
                [32m'`Ash.Changeset.for_destroy(record, :archive, %{})` and\n'[39m +
                [32m'`Ash.Changeset.for_update(record, :restore, %{})`.\n'[39m +
                [32m'\n'[39m +
                [32m'### Archive semantics — action `:archive`\n'[39m +
                [32m'\n'[39m +
                [32m'* Nothing is ever removed from storage by `:archive`.\n'[39m +
                [32m'* If the target record is already archived, the call still succeeds but nothing changes anywhere:\n'[39m +
                [32m'  the target keeps its existing `archived_at` and `archive_batch_id`, and no descendant is modified.\n'[39m +
                [32m"* Otherwise the target and every descendant of the target that is not already archived (a post's\n"[39m +
                [32m"  comments and those comments' reactions; a comment's reactions) are archived together as one\n"[39m +
                [32m'  generation: all of them end up with the *same* non-`nil` `archived_at` value and the *same*\n'[39m +
                [32m'  non-`nil` `archive_batch_id` value.\n'[39m +
                [32m'* Descendants that were already archived before the call keep their existing `archived_at` and\n'[39m +
                [32m'  `archive_batch_id` values byte-for-byte.\n'[39m +
                [32m'* Two separate archive operations must never produce the same `archive_batch_id`.\n'[39m +
                [32m'\n'[39m +
                [32m'### Restore semantics — action `:restore`\n'[39m +
                [32m'\n'[39m +
                [32m'* On a record that is not archived the call succeeds and changes nothing, anywhere.\n'[39m +
                [32m"* On an archived record: the target's `archived_at` and `archive_batch_id` both become `nil`, and\n"[39m +
                [32m"  every descendant whose `archive_batch_id` equals the target's `archive_batch_id` as it was\n"[39m +
                [32m'  immediately before the call is restored the same way (`archived_at` and `archive_batch_id` set to\n'[39m +
                [32m'  `nil`), recursively.\n'[39m +
                [32m'* Descendants carrying a different `archive_batch_id` are left exactly as they were.\n'[39m +
                [32m'* `:restore` never affects ancestors of the target.\n'[39m +
                [32m'\n'[39m +
                [32m'### Purge semantics — action `:purge`\n'[39m +
                [32m'\n'[39m +
                [32m'* Invoked on a record whose `archived_at` is `nil`, the action must fail and change nothing: the\n'[39m +
                [32m'  result must be `{:error, %Ash.Error.Invalid{errors: errors}}` where at least one element of\n'[39m +
                [32m'  `errors` is an `%Ash.Error.Changes.InvalidChanges{}` whose `:fields` is `[:archived_at]` and whose\n'[39m +
                [32m'  `:message` is exactly `"must be archived before it can be purged"`.\n'[39m +
                [32m'* Invoked on an archived record, the record and every one of its descendants are permanently and\n'[39m +
                [32m'  irrecoverably removed from storage.\n'[39m +
                [32m'\n'[39m +
                [32m'### Read scoping\n'[39m +

            [32m'# Committing changes with git\n'[39m +

            [32m'Git Safety Protocol:\n'[39m +

Taking unauthorized destructive actions is unhelpful and can result in lost work, so it's best to ONLY run these commands when given direct instructions \n"[39m +
